title: BUILD-entry isolation — deterministic closure of the BUILD boundary under a request-time configuration guard
status: DRAFT v3 — additive revision per the final preregistration review (architecture APPROVED; three evidence-path corrections implemented); NOT binding until approved; live execution remains unauthorized
directive: Operator P2 forensic closure (binding v5 accepted at 4c124b0): GO to P3 design and offline qualification only. Build and qualify a deterministic BUILD-entry fixture with a request-time configuration guard; preregister P3; execute only after separate review.

motivation.p2_outcome: UNEVALUABLE_FOR_ENDPOINT — 9/9 workflow slots, 0 BUILD opportunities; additionally the frozen per-step budgets never reached any request (campaign driver seed() overwrote the frozen settings), so P2 measured a degraded regime, not the preregistered one
motivation.lesson_1: the runtime must verify EFFECTIVE configuration — the invariant is what reaches the provider request, not the settings file on disk
motivation.lesson_2: upstream workflow reliability and BUILD protocol reliability are separate measurements; a full-workflow campaign can exhaust its budget without testing its intervention
motivation.lesson_3: provider observability must include resolved execution parameters (outbound max_tokens, reasoning configuration, routing), not only schemas and responses

research_question: Given valid upstream inputs and the intended runtime configuration, how reliably can Stratum's BUILD protocol produce and publish an authorized change?
treatment: BUILD Edit Protocol v1.1 (frozen, unchanged from P2-B): anchored semantic edits via submit_result, narrowed edits-only surface, deterministic staging + composition evidence, unchanged publication boundary

verification_points: construction: settings sha256 == frozen 5634b2e8 (the P2 defect class cannot recur silently)

every completeMultiTurn request, BEFORE forwarding: model, max_tokens (frozen per-step value), reasoning.effort (presence AND value), temperature, tool-name set (investigation vs synthesis shapes), submit_result surface (narrowed: edits-only, required [edits], no creates) with LINE-FORM teaching markers (`- /properties/edits: ` present, `- /properties/creates: ` absent) scanned across ALL model-visible user messages and the system prompt, non-empty system + messages
tools_sha256: recursive deterministic serialization of the FULL tool definitions — every material schema mutation changes the hash (6/6 proven in Q1)

complete and completeStructured are EXPLICITLY BLOCKED (fail closed pre-call; the attempt is archived as a guard STOP naming the denied wire) — the guarded multi-turn wire is the only channel in P3 scope

every verified request is archived BEFORE the verdict is applied, followed by its response — full text + sha + stop_reason + usage PLUS the verbatim wire_observation (finish_reason, prompt/completion/reasoning/total token counts, provider, stream identity, content/reasoning byte counts, reasoning fields, tool-call fragments) — the P2 wire-capture composition, so a future transport-censoring decision (the P2 class: stop_reason end_turn + finish_reason error + partial content) has independent response-side evidence; the anomalous class is qualified in Q6a
any mismatch -> 'config-guard: STOP — ...' and the model call is NEVER made; classification: experiment STOP (config-guard class G1), never a model failure

ARCHIVAL/PROVIDER SEPARATION: provider execution failures archive an error record; response/error-record WRITE failures throw an evidence-integrity ConfigGuardViolation (G2 class) and are never recorded as provider errors — the provider call can never be misrepresented by an archival defect (qualified in Q6b); the same fail-closed rule applies to blocked-completion archival
request_time_configuration_guard.campaign_recognition: after EVERY attempt the campaign classifies the attempt capture (classifyGuardCapture): config/completion-path guard STOPs -> G1 STOP; evidence-integrity STOPs, pairing/parse defects, or reconciliation mismatches -> G2 STOP; archival failures are structurally distinguishable from provider failures; both classes demonstrated in Q5/Q6 on real capture shapes

primary_endpoint.statement: With the entry fixture and the request-time guard in force, BUILD stages and publishes its required authorized source edit in at least 2 of 3 BUILD-entry attempts
primary_endpoint.publication_definition: identical to P1-R/P2: submit_result accepted -> staged -> publication gates passed -> applied-edit provenance row written AND disk bytes == provenance hash
primary_endpoint.decision_rule: >=2/3 publications => SUPPORTED; <=1/3 => FALSIFIED; guard STOP, evidence-integrity failure, authority bypass, surface-binding failure, or target drift => STOP and return to the operator (never a model-attributed failure)
primary_endpoint.denominator_rule: each attempt = one fixture instantiation + confirm-gate approval + one BUILD execution. A config-guard STOP, capture-integrity failure, or fixture-restore failure consumes NO attempt (procedure class, re-queue after operator-visible journal entry). A model-caused BUILD failure (submission rejection, repair exhaustion, staging rejection) IS an evaluable attempt (P1-R precedent). Transport failure mid-BUILD: journal + re-queue, consumes no attempt (addendum-2 discipline: ambiguity is NOT censored; the archived capture decides).
primary_endpoint.deliberate_divergence_from_p2: P3 does NOT inherit P2's full-workflow sampling plan (9 workflows). The denominator is BUILD-entry attempts only; upstream progression is out of scope by construction.
primary_endpoint.execution_boundary: POSITIVE publication halt: the campaign runs BUILD under a boundary wrapper that refuses every step dispatch after BUILD completes — the run halts at the first downstream step with an explicit sentinel BEFORE any downstream model call or side effect (proven in Q4: exactly 1 refusal, 0 downstream requests, work tree carries only the publication). A rejected downstream request is never part of the procedure.

per_attempt_reporting_fields: wire_surface_offered (from the guard capture: tools, full-def tools_sha256, submit_result schema, line-form teaching markers, message counts)
resolved parameters per request (model, max_tokens, reasoning_effort, temperature) — guard-verified pre-call
provider responses and errors (full text sha + bytes, stop_reason, usage, tool-use names, duration) — archived per request
submission outcome (accepted / rejected + defects) and repair consumption
publication outcome (applied-edit row sha, disk==provenance verification)
capture reconciliation (archived PASS count == provider call count; classifyGuardCapture verdict)
post-publication target state (HEAD, main.py sha, tree cleanliness) and the boundary refusal evidence

stop_rules.G1_config_guard: any config-guard STOP during a BUILD attempt (request-time violation OR blocked completion path) -> STOP campaign, return to operator; classified from the capture after the attempt (demonstrated Q5a)
stop_rules.G2_evidence_integrity: capture write failure, pairing/parse defect, reconciliation mismatch, dual-failure class, or composition-evidence absence -> STOP (S2 class; tamper detection demonstrated Q5b)
stop_rules.G3_surface_binding: archived requests showing a creates-bearing submit_result -> STOP (S3 class)
stop_rules.G4_target_drift: HEAD != 86ec0871 or main.py != 7d7718bc at attempt start or after restore -> STOP (S4 class)
stop_rules.G5_capability_regression: preflight fail or supported_efforts losing 'low' -> STOP (S5 class)
stop_rules.G6_fixture_restore: definition/readiness sha mismatch or boundary-property verification failure on instantiate -> STOP (S6 class)

scope_boundaries.in_scope: BUILD entry -> investigation -> structured submission -> validation -> publication; the downstream workflow (exec/validation_gate/debug/evaluate) is NOT driven — after publication the target is restored pristine
scope_boundaries.out_of_scope: upstream progression (P4's question), downstream test outcomes (do not un-publish, P1-R precedent), model quality beyond the protocol boundary
